parts.note: put either colour in front and you get a familiar hedgerow bush, the black one bearing sloes and the white one being ...

explanation.surface: A gardener's question about whether a bush is the dark or the pale variety.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackthorn and whitethorn (hawthorn) are both spiny bushes, and the shared word names that kind of prickly shrub.

clue.text: Cruisers Gloucester and Carlisle for instance ?

definitions.text: Cruisers Gloucester and Carlisle for instance ?

parts.words: Cruisers Gloucester and Carlisle for instance
parts.note: warships named after English cities, so vessels bearing the names of urban places

explanation.surface: A naval list of Royal Navy cruisers named after English cities.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as TOWN SHIPS: ships named after towns. Gloucester and Carlisle are English cathedral cities.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase also names settlements, especially South African urban areas, while the split reading names vessels called after places.

definitions.meaning: to arrange things is to put them in sequence
the roster of members of the Bath, the British chivalric honour

explanation.definitionFit: To arrange is to put into sequence; the Bath is a British chivalric society, a brotherhood of knights.

clue.text: Approaching a circle from two directions

parts.note: N and E are the compass points north and east
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: Someone closes in on a roundabout from two sides at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' just says the circle comes after the directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming nearer to something is drawing close to it.

clue.text: In this respect it can't mean postponement

definitions.text: In this respect it can't mean postponement

parts.words: In this respect it can't mean postponement
parts.note: the word for respect looks as if it comes from defer in the sense of putting off, but here it is the other sense, yielding to someone

explanation.surface: A pedant insisting a word must not be taken to mean delay.
explanation.walkthrough: To defer can mean to put off or to yield to someone; the noun meaning respect comes from the yielding sense, not the delaying one, which gives deferment.
explanation.definitionFit: Courteous regard for a superior's wishes is respectful submission.

parts.note: a large moth has a skull-like marking on its thorax, and is named for that head

explanation.surface: A naturalist's remark that a particular head marking tells you which moth it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The death's-head hawkmoth has a skull pattern on its back; the clue asks for the word before 'head'.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull marking on the hawkmoth gives it the name 'death's-head', which this word completes.

clue.text: No charge for autumn parachute show

parts.note: something with no charge is free
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: An autumn air display of parachuting that costs nothing to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Skydivers drop without opening their canopies for a time, a display of descent under gravity alone.

clue.text: Engineers' code shows sense of guilt

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps
Morse is the telegraph code of dots and dashes

explanation.surface: Army signallers' coded messages reveal a troubled conscience.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep regret for wrongdoing is a feeling of guilt.

clue.text: Not the type for a peerage!

definitions.text: Not the type for a peerage!

parts.words: Not the type for a peerage!
parts.note: the word means having no equal, no peer, and is also the name of a small printing type size

explanation.surface: Someone judged unsuitable to be made a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'type' is a size of printing type, and 'not for a peerage' reads as 'without a peer', which is what the French-derived word means.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without equal is unrivalled; the same word was an old name for six-point printing type.

parts.note: split as corn-ish listeners: corn has ears, the grain heads, so this means having ears

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone in Cornwall is within earshot.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's south-western tip, but 'Cornish' here means of corn: a stalk of corn bears ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Possessing ears, whether of hearing or of grain, describes a plant or creature with them.

parts.note: a broad-brimmed soft felt hat whose name also means fully alert, the vigilant sort

explanation.surface: Asking what hat a self-appointed crime fighter wears.
explanation.walkthrough: The hat's name doubles as the phrase for being vigilant, and 'Vigilante' hides 'vigilant'.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-crowned felt hat has the same name as the phrase for being fully alert.

parts.note: the old Royal Sappers and ... paired sappers with diggers of tunnels

explanation.surface: An old soldier's friend from his army engineering days.
explanation.walkthrough: A sapper digs trenches or saps; the Royal Sappers and Miners was the old name of the British army's engineer corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who digs underground for coal or to undermine fortifications worked alongside sappers.

definitions.meaning: a footballer who plays as a forward and runs directly at goal is a ...

explanation.definitionFit: A player in an attacking position playing directly, and also candid and uncomplicated.

clue.text: Chilly period for much of Europe

definitions.text: Chilly period for much of Europe

parts.words: Chilly period for much of Europe
parts.note: an era when glaciers covered northern Europe

explanation.surface: A weather forecast warning of a cold spell across the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacial epoch was a prolonged spell of cold when ice sheets spread over large areas.

clue.text: So pawn takes pawn, by the way

definitions.meaning: the chess capture in which a pawn takes a pawn that has just moved two squares past it
a French phrase used in English to mean incidentally

explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means in passing, naming a chess capture and meaning incidentally.

definitions.meaning: dormant ones are those that sleep; a noun plural against an adjective
railway beams lie under the track, supporting the train: 'training' read as train-ing

explanation.definitionFit: Those who slumber, and the wooden or concrete railway beams that hold the rails beneath trains.

definitions.meaning: to give up something to another

explanation.definitionFit: To relinquish or give up, and as a noun the act of capitulation.

clue.text: Rower trips awkwardly in front of boat

parts.note: bow is the oarsman seated nearest the front of a rowing boat

indicators.note: the letters of trips are moved about clumsily into a new order

explanation.surface: An oarsman stumbles clumsily at the front of the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The spar projecting forward from a vessel's prow is the one out in front.

clue.text: For mother the lake is better

definitions.meaning: the head of a convent is Mother ...
Lake ... is the largest of North America's Great Lakes

explanation.definitionFit: It completes the convent head's title, names the biggest Great Lake, and means of higher quality.

parts.note: the uppermost part of a building is its covering roof

explanation.surface: Asking about the topmost thing that covers a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper surface of a building's covering is its highest point.

parts.note: to shadow someone is to tail them, follow closely

explanation.surface: Two names offered as alternatives, as if picking between characters.
explanation.walkthrough: Starveling is the tailor among the craftsmen in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's comedy Starveling is a clothes-maker by trade.

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the artist's letters upwards, so they are read backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
a rival is a competitor

explanation.surface: A painter is unsettled by a rival on the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving somewhere is the act of reaching it, a coming.

definitions.meaning: living off others like a cadger, as one who sponges

explanation.definitionFit: Absorbent like a bath sponge, and in a playful sense cadging like a freeloader.

clue.text: Somewhere wild American is well-mounted at the seaside

parts.note: the Wild West of America
a rider who is well mounted is on a super mare

explanation.surface: An American horseman of the Wild West is splendidly mounted beside the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The town is a seaside resort in Somerset, England; 'at the seaside' tells you what sort of place it is. Its Latin 'super Mare' means on sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort town on the Bristol Channel is a place, a location.

clue.text: A cool cat, her novels will amuse, you see

indicators.note: says the answer can be seen within the words will and amuse

explanation.surface: A trendy feline's novels are said to be entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A cool cat, her' read with 'cool' as C sounds like 'A Cather': Willa Cather was an American novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Willa Cather wrote My Antonia; the first name is identified by her novels.

indicators.note: confusion jumbles the letters into a new order

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Muddle about fifty singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Voices pitched high among men or low among women are singers of a particular range.

parts.note: points to the proverb about the less said the soonest mended

explanation.surface: A remark that saying this makes mending fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'least said, soonest mended': the clue puts the missing first word in front of 'said'.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest amount is the opening word of the proverb about soonest mended.

clue.text: It's about the new star, Edward, after the Restoration

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens, from the Latin for new
Ted is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A story about a new star called Edward in the period after 1660.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Restoration' looks like the 1660 return of Charles II; read it as a restoring job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done up again has been restored, so it is in the state that follows restoring.

clue.text: There's opposition to pay, in that disorder

indicators.note: the words pay, in and that are thrown into disarray

explanation.surface: Opponents are against paying, amid the chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep dislike is hostility, a feeling against something.

indicators.note: difficult here means the word roles is made awkward and reshuffled

explanation.surface: An actor is defeated by hard parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The one who is defeated in a contest is the one who does not win.
